record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: Which vector bundles compute the Clifford index Cliff_n(C), and among them which, if any, are stable bundles?

evidence.quote: Question 3.8. Which bundles compute the Clifford index? Which, if any, stable bundles do so?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth irreducible complex projective curve of genus $g\geq 2$. For a vector bundle $E$ on $C$ of rank $n$ and degree $d$, define the Clifford index of $E$ by
$$\gamma(E) \;=\; \mu(E) - \frac{2}{n}\,h^0(E) + 2 \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\bigl(d - 2(h^0(E)-n)\bigr),$$
where $\mu(E)=d/n$ is the slope. For an integer $n\geq 1$, the rank-$n$ Clifford index of $C$ is
$$\mathrm{Cliff}_n(C) \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\gamma(E) \;:\; E \text{ semistable of rank } n,\ h^0(E)\geq 2n,\ \mu(E)\leq g-1 \bigr\}.$$
A semistable bundle $E$ attaining this infimum is said to compute $\mathrm{Cliff}_n(C)$.

Problem. Characterize the semistable vector bundles $E$ of rank $n$ on $C$ that compute $\mathrm{Cliff}_n(C)$. In particular, determine for which curves $C$ and which ranks $n$ there exists a stable bundle computing $\mathrm{Cliff}_n(C)$, and describe all such stable bundles when they exist.
artifact.category_tag: Higher rank Clifford index of curves
artifact.status_search_result: The question of which (semi)stable bundles compute the higher rank Clifford index of a curve, and whether stable ones do, remains an active research topic. Partial results exist for small ranks: for rank 2, bundles computing the index are known to be linearly semistable, and for curves of Clifford dimension at least 3 such a bundle has been shown to be stable and of Lazarsfeld–Mukai type; recent work (2025) and prior work treat rank 2 and rank 3 on special curves (e.g. on K3 surfaces), but no general classification is known.

status_evidence.title: Linear stability and rank two Clifford indices of algebraic curves
status_evidence.snippet: Any vector bundle computing the rank-two Clifford index of a smooth projective algebraic curve is linearly semistable.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work obtains partial structural results in rank 2, showing the problem is still being actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Vector Bundles of Rank 2 Computing Clifford Indices
status_evidence.snippet: For curves of Clifford dimension r ≥ 3, any rank-2 semistable bundle computing γ_2 is a Lazarsfeld–Mukai bundle and is stable.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification known in rank 2 under additional hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Higher rank Clifford indices of curves on a K3 surface
status_evidence.snippet: The rank r-Clifford index can be computed by the restriction of the corresponding Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundle on surfaces in certain cases.
status_evidence.claim: Only special-case computations are available; no general answer.
